title: Methanol poisoning (toxic alcohol)
subject: toxicology
summary: Suspect methanol after illicit liquor with high anion gap acidosis or visual symptoms. Start fomepizole or ethanol on suspicion, correct acidosis with bicarbonate, give folic or folinic acid, and haemodialyse early for severe poisoning (EXTRIP 2015).

sections.title: Recognise
items: Sources in India: illicit or spurious liquor (often outbreaks with many cases), industrial solvents and adulterated sanitisers.

Latent period of 12 to 24 hours (longer if ethanol was drunk too), then headache, vomiting, abdominal pain, breathlessness (Kussmaul breathing), blurred or 'snowfield' vision, blindness, seizures and coma.
High anion gap metabolic acidosis. The osmolar gap is high early but falls as methanol is converted to formate, so a normal gap does not exclude late poisoning.
Anyone who drank from the same source needs assessment even if well.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Blood gas (pH, bicarbonate, lactate), electrolytes, anion gap (Na minus (Cl plus HCO3)), glucose, creatinine, CK and amylase.

Measured osmolality (freezing point depression) and calculated osmolarity: 2 x Na + glucose (mg/dL)/18 + BUN (mg/dL)/2.8 (or urea mg/dL/6); add ethanol (mg/dL)/3.7 if present. An osmolar gap above 10 mOsm/kg supports a toxic alcohol.
Serum methanol and ethanol by gas chromatography where available (and formate); do not delay treatment waiting for them.
Fundoscopy (disc hyperaemia or oedema); CT brain in coma (putaminal necrosis or haemorrhage).

sections.title: Immediate management
items: ABC; intubate for coma. If ventilated, match the patient's high minute ventilation to avoid worsening acidosis.
Start an alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) blocker immediately on clinical suspicion (credible history plus unexplained high anion gap acidosis or osmolar gap).
Activated charcoal and gastric lavage are not useful: methanol is absorbed quickly and is not adsorbed by charcoal.
In outbreaks, start ethanol or fomepizole in all suspected cases and triage dialysis by severity (acidosis, coma, visual loss).

sections.title: ADH blockade: fomepizole or ethanol
items: Indications: methanol 20 mg/dL (6.2 mmol/L) or more, or suspected ingestion with at least 2 of: arterial pH below 7.3, bicarbonate below 20 mmol/L, osmolar gap above 10 mOsm/kg.

Fomepizole (preferred where available): 15 mg/kg IV loading, then 10 mg/kg every 12 hours for 4 doses, then 15 mg/kg every 12 hours. During haemodialysis give doses every 4 hours, or an infusion of 1 to 1.5 mg/kg/h.
Ethanol when fomepizole is unavailable (common in India), in ICU: IV 10% ethanol 10 mL/kg loading, then 1 mL/kg/h; or orally 1 mL/kg of 96% ethanol diluted fivefold as loading, then 0.16 mL/kg/h.

Target serum ethanol 100 to 150 mg/dL (22 to 33 mmol/L): check the level after loading and every 1 to 2 hours and titrate (chronic drinkers often need higher maintenance), increase maintenance (about double) during haemodialysis, and monitor glucose and sedation.
Continue until methanol is below 20 mg/dL, or if levels are unavailable, until the acidosis has resolved and the osmolar gap has normalised.

sections.title: Bicarbonate, folate and haemodialysis
items: Sodium bicarbonate IV for significant acidosis (pH below 7.3), aiming for pH above 7.2; it reduces formate entry into tissues. Watch sodium, potassium and fluid overload.
Folic acid 1 mg/kg (maximum 50 mg) IV every 4 hours, or folinic acid (leucovorin), to enhance formate metabolism; continue during dialysis.
EXTRIP haemodialysis indications (any one): coma, seizures, new visual deficits, pH 7.15 or less, persistent acidosis despite treatment, anion gap above 24 mmol/L, or impaired kidney function.
EXTRIP methanol thresholds for dialysis: above 700 mg/L (70 mg/dL) with fomepizole, above 600 mg/L (60 mg/dL) with ethanol, above 500 mg/L (50 mg/dL) without an ADH blocker.
Intermittent haemodialysis is the modality of choice. Continue the ADH blocker and folate during dialysis; stop dialysis when methanol is below 200 mg/L (20 mg/dL) with clinical improvement.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: Blood gas, electrolytes and osmolality every few hours until acidosis resolves; recheck after dialysis for rebound.
On ethanol: serum ethanol every 1 to 2 hours, hourly glucose, and level of consciousness.
Record visual acuity and fundi; long-term sequelae include blindness and parkinsonism from putaminal necrosis.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting for a methanol level before starting an ADH blocker.
Excluding methanol because the osmolar gap is normal in a late presenter.
Ethanol therapy without level monitoring (under-dosing, hypoglycaemia, oversedation).
Stopping ethanol or fomepizole at the end of dialysis without rechecking levels or acidosis.

drugs.name: Fomepizole
drugs.dose: 15 mg/kg IV loading, then 10 mg/kg every 12 hours for 4 doses, then 15 mg/kg every 12 hours
drugs.notes: During haemodialysis dose every 4 hours or infuse 1 to 1.5 mg/kg/h.

drugs.name: Ethanol 10% IV
drugs.notes: Target serum ethanol 100 to 150 mg/dL; increase during dialysis; ICU monitoring.

drugs.name: Ethanol oral
drugs.dose: 1 mL/kg of 96% ethanol diluted fivefold as loading, then 0.16 mL/kg/h
drugs.notes: Orally or by nasogastric tube when IV ethanol and fomepizole are unavailable.

drugs.name: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4%
drugs.dose: IV boluses or infusion titrated to blood gas, aiming for pH above 7.2
drugs.notes: Monitor sodium, potassium and volume status.
